Independently found by architect, security-guardian, compliance-officer, sre, enterprise-readiness, and unhappy-path (UP-1).

trigger: a Guardian RegistryGuard log statement prints cfg_.value_type, which is operator-authored free text (param("value_type")), not a closed-set/compile-time literal as an earlier exemption comment claimed
summary: cfg_.value_type reached spdlog raw at 2 sites, the same trust boundary as hive/key/value_name/expected (already wrapped by the prior adversarial-review round) -- a sibling-field miss.

trigger: upsert_rule_status and both insert_event_classified/insert_events observation-projection-failure logs print agent_id, which is client-supplied at Register (length-checked only), charset-unrestricted
summary: agent_id reached spdlog raw at 3 sites, on the same lines where the adjacent rule_id/event_id were already wrapped. A prior commit (3784a6f21) deferred this to issue #489, which on re-check does not cover this file or this class of site -- the deferral was a miscitation, not a settled scope decision.

trigger: a future spdlog::warn(fmt::format("...{}...", rule_id)) call (no current instance in the tree, verified by grep)
summary: parse_call() requires the statement's first token after ( to be a bare string literal; a spdlog call wrapping a pre-built fmt::format(...) string entirely evades detection, silently returning zero violations. No live instance today. Re-derived MEDIUM/SHOULD (not the reporter's native HIGH) since IMPACT is a forward-looking scanner-coverage gap against no current forgery sink, not a live vulnerability.
adjudication_rationale: Downgraded from reporter's native HIGH to derived SHOULD: TRIGGER requires a future call site that does not exist today (grep-confirmed), so IMPACT is I7 (missing/incomplete limitation documentation) rather than a live I1-I3 class defect. Disposed by documenting the limitation plainly in the scanner's own module docstring (matching the file's established convention for its other known limitation, degrade_msg) rather than extending the scanner's parser -- Gate 7 Test 1/2: no live forgery sink exists to fix, so this is scanner-hardening against a future regression class, tracked in-file per this repo's stated convention rather than filed as a separate issue.

trigger: a legacy rule_id that is charset-clean ([A-Za-z0-9._-]+) but exceeds 256 bytes (creatable only pre-#4665, when creation had no length bound either)
summary: upgrading.md claimed REST DELETE can't reach a non-conforming rule_id and MCP delete_guardian_rule has no such restriction -- backwards for a charset-clean-but-over-256-byte id: REST's route regex has no length bound so it CAN delete it; MCP's own schema caps at maxLength:256 and the #2405 validation gate rejects the call before the handler runs, so MCP CAN'T.

trigger: a release-notes reader or procurement contact scanning assembled CHANGELOG.md for a Breaking lead phrase
summary: the changelog fragment buried its breaking whole-push-reject behavior change three sentences deep with no bolded **Breaking --** lead, unlike the repo's own repeated precedent for this shape of change (CHANGELOG.md lines 59, 2122 etc).

trigger: a pilot operator with months of REST-automation-created Guardian rules (no prior charset enforcement) about to upgrade
summary: upgrading.md said to find and remove a non-conforming legacy rule_id before upgrading but gave no query/script to find one, despite GET /api/v1/guaranteed-state/rules trivially supporting a client-side filter against the documented charset.

trigger: a legacy non-conforming rule_id in scope of a repeatedly-reconciling agent (25s floor, server.cpp)
summary: UP-3: a stuck legacy rule caused an indefinite steady-state loop -- every reconcile interval, every in-scope lagging agent re-receives the identical poisoned push, re-rejects, re-emits the rejection line, forever, with no reject-aware backoff. Resolved as a side effect of the guardian_push_builder.cpp server-side filter: the agent no longer receives the poisoned push at all in the ordinary case.

trigger: a bump_policy_generation_on call landing strictly between the heartbeat-reconcile closure's separate, non-transactional current_policy_generation() and list_rules() reads
summary: UP-5: a generation bump landing between the two reads could tag a push with a newer generation than the rule content it carries, silently dropping a rule from that push until an unrelated later generation bump retries it. Not reproduced empirically, traced from source.

trigger: an audit_fn throw on the REST create-deny path for an invalid rule_id
summary: UP-8: REST's new create-deny audit call is bare (no try/catch), unlike MCP's equivalent path which wraps via try_persist_audit -- matches the file's pre-existing sibling asymmetry (also flagged by security-guardian), not a regression introduced by #4665, but this PR had the opportunity to align REST with MCP's safer pattern.

trigger: reading the tripwire's exemption comment for guard_registry.cpp's cfg_.value_type bracket

Moot once value_type was wrapped and the exemption/comment removed.

trigger: a hostile system-bus peer controlling an sd-bus error-name reply to LoadUnit/ActiveState
summary: err.name (an sd-bus error-name string) is logged unwrapped alongside the now-wrapped uw.unit -- not operator-authored per #4665's stated threat model, only attacker-influenceable via a hostile system-bus peer, a narrower/speculative surface. Not fixed in this pass -- out of #4665's stated scope (operator-authored fields), noted for a future hardening look, not filed given its narrow/speculative nature.
adjudication_rationale: EXPOSURE requires a hostile system-bus peer (E5, rare environmental/adversarial condition well outside #4665's stated threat model of operator-authored strings); IMPACT is I9 (no operational impact within this PR's scope). Left as a plainly-noted future-hardening observation rather than filed, since it is speculative and narrow enough that a tracked issue would add process overhead disproportionate to the finding.
